findings.explicit_hold: Output semantics and 26/26 historical engineering checks accepted; unconditional performance adoption held. The latest substantive review asks to avoid per-statement large JSON membership reconstruction, then evaluate current-source dense/sparse/multi-batch wall/rows/VM including Rust JSON allocation. The latest administrative comment retains Draft and says no representative equivalent end-to-end benefit yet.

exact_production.mechanism: serde_json::to_string happens once per call at 136-140; the same parameter is bound to a NOT IN (SELECT value FROM json_each(...)) for each kind/key batch at 145-176. prepare_cached caches a prepared statement, not proof that the bound membership results survive executions.

actual_evidence.historical_CI: G4 run37947395888; all26 success per retained independent review. Nine DB tests and original v15 passed; current work did not redownload logs.
actual_evidence.exact_G4_dense: 600 rows/580 exclusions: output parity, rows590->10, test asserted lower VM; successful log has no numeric VM and no paired Rust wall.

minimum_now: Documentation-only: put current Draft/performance-HOLD first; retain earlier ready/pending passages explicitly as history and separate the M7 five-file numbers from exact G4. Keep no 100k-timeout-fix claim.

A new production candidate, if desired, must solve or avoid membership rebuilding rather than merely cache the existing prepared statement or move the existing once-per-call serialization. A read-lease-compatible design is required; do not introduce TEMP-table writes or a guessed density threshold as an unreviewed shortcut.

Before adopting a claimed optimization, prepare an exact-current-source finite mechanism comparison retaining dense, sparse and multi-batch negatives, full outputs and setup/serialization/allocation cost. This is a proposed next separate experiment, not a request to rerun the original registered scale study.
findings.not_safely_concluded_now: No small code change can be certified to remove the performance HOLD from existing results alone. A finite redesigned mechanism result could support a limited adoption decision; it would not prove the historical five-hour failure fixed or establish current-source scale speed.
findings.parallelism: Can prepare documentation/design independently of190/191; any new bindings must be based on the actual new composition, not copied from the old fixed-base PR.

findings.head: 7da43a80bc00698101de5619dd486a3393a667a3
findings.explicit_hold: Current-main engineering correctness accepted on its fixed source; performance adoption held because four cost cases have mixed direction and order association, no full-rebuild improvement. No requirement for an additional full scale study is stated in this review.

actual_evidence.CI: 37963897699/check113933295910 completed success; six new controls actual pass, old ignored cost probe remains ignored. Later MSRV/security success recorded in body; no repeated log download.

findings.confirmed_probe_boundary: cost_round lines364-382 times inserts only, then returns full base/FTS row vectors after readback and rollback. At417-427 the first returned row vectors remain live during the second timing. Warm reference vectors also remain in scope equally. This adds a possible allocator/state asymmetry to already observed order dependence; causal size is unknown.
findings.custody_boundary: Published original intake explicitly says original observer hashed its actual ELF but original ZIP contains no ELF, so a later independent rehash cannot be obtained merely by reopening that ZIP. Earlier comment's 'ELF not yet independently accepted' must not turn into an impossible retrospective requirement or a false seal claim.
minimum_now: Documentation-only: append the exact ELF-unavailable boundary and timing/readback lifetime asymmetry to existing HOLD while preserving all80 records and the historical comment.
Use the already available by_first10/10 distributions when assessing the local claim. Do not pool cases, trim rounds, invent a threshold or assert end-to-end gains.

If preparing a future diagnostic patch, add a separately named ignored probe with symmetric per-side readback/output lifetimes and common untimed equality reference; retain existing timer boundaries and original probe. This can be authored/reviewed without running a full study, but no new results exist yet.

No production fix is justified solely by the small noisy timings: lazy initialization, error cleanup and per-file statement lifetime are already implemented and tested. Do not add a guessed chunk-count activation cutoff.

Any eventual current-main integration must merge retained-statement changes with main's existing immutable-payload/prevalidated-frontier changes in the same write_batch file; replacing the file wholesale with the old PR would lose adopted work.
findings.parallelism: The documentation and separately named probe preparation can proceed alongside190; product integration into main needs an explicit same-file merge review and actual future CI. No study/ref action here.

recommended_order: 190:reuse existing equal-lifetime candidate, no duplicate implementation
191:document custody/lifetime limits and prepare symmetric probe only if desired
188:keep production adoption held; document adverse results and design read-only membership alternative before new cost evidence
